SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

AI TUTOR, AMHARIC - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help train and refine Grok's voice and language capabilities in Amharic. Your expertise will directly shape how Grok speaks and understands Amharic, from pronunciation and natural phrasing to cultural nuance. You will see your work show up in a product used by people around the world.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Annotate, label, and provide feedback on multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, and speech samples using proprietary tools

Translate and localize text (UI copy, prompts, responses, and other content) from English into Amharic, with attention to accuracy, natural phrasing, and cultural fit

Help produce clear, natural audio data that accurately captures linguistic and prosodic details such as intonation, rhythm, and accent

Collaborate with technical staff to refine annotation guidelines and tools for handling accents, background noise, speech variation, and multilingual audio

POSITION DETAILS:

This is a temporary position with SpaceXSI, for the length of time as stated, and is subject to change with minimal notice as business needs dictate

LENGTH OF POSITION: 6 months (extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs)

LOCATION: Remote (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia); for US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Proficiency in Amharic at CEFR C1 level or higher

English proficiency at CEFR B2 level or higher

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Native proficiency in Amharic

English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher

Experience in one or more of the following areas: 

Advanced transcription or audio annotation, with strong attention to accents, prosody, disfluencies, and variable recording quality

Translation or localization work (especially UI, product copy, or conversational text) between English and Amharic

Voice recording, voice acting, podcasting, or related audio production that demonstrates clear delivery and attention to sound quality

Background in linguistics, phonetics, speech sciences, or hands-on work with speech/audio datasets and AI training data

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

This role may be offered as a full-time or part-time position depending on role/business needs and candidate availability; full-time positions are preferred and require working standard business hours in your local time zone

We are unable to provide visa sponsorship

Must be willing to travel to a SpaceXSI site

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

US-based candidates: $35/hour - $45/hour depending on factors including relevant experience, skills, education, geographic location, and qualifications. International candidates: Information will be provided to you during the recruitment process.

Benefits vary based on employment type, location, and jurisdiction. Benefits for eligible US-based positions include health insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid sick leave. Specific details and role-specific information will be provided to you during the interview process.

AI TUTOR, APPLIED MATH - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by providing high-quality data annotations, labels, and inputs focused on applied mathematics. You will draw on your expertise in areas such as numerical analysis and scientific computing, ordinary and partial differential equations, probability and applied statistics, computational linear algebra, and mathematical physics or mathematical biology to evaluate model outputs, identify modeling errors or numerical issues, and produce clear, rigorous solutions and explanations. This role requires strong mathematical writing skills, attention to precision, and the ability to maintain logical consistency throughout complex mathematical arguments. Your work will help train Grok to distinguish flawed or inadequately justified approaches from solutions that are mathematically sound, accurately modeled, and practically applicable.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Evaluate model outputs, independently verify mathematical solutions, identify subtle errors in reasoning, modelling, or numerical computations, and produce clear, rigorous, and technically sound solutions and explanations

Use proprietary software applications to annotate and label data for designated projects

Support the delivery of high-quality, accurate, and well-curated datasets that meet project standards

Collaborate with technical teams to develop and train new tasks, contributing to the successful development and implementation of innovative technologies and initiatives

Work closely with technical staff to improve the design, functionality, and efficiency of annotation tools and workflows

Solve problems across applied mathematics domains aligned with your expertise, including probability, statistics, numerical analysis, optimization, operations research, dynamical systems, data modeling, and related fields. Develop detailed solutions and critically evaluate AI-generated responses

Interpret, analyze, and execute tasks accurately in accordance with established guidelines and project requirements

POSITION DETAILS:

This is a temporary position with SpaceXSI, for the length of time as stated, and is subject to change with minimal notice as business needs dictate

LENGTH OF POSITION: 6 months (extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs)

LOCATION: Remote (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and India); for US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Master’s degree or Ph.D. in mathematics, with a specialization in an applied mathematics subfield; OR a medal in the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) or a comparable high-level mathematics competition

English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Peer-reviewed publications in applied mathematics in reputable scientific journals

Previous experience in AI tutoring, AI model evaluation, or related applications of artificial intelligence

Teaching experience, particularly at the college or university level

Strong research skills, including the ability to navigate diverse information resources, academic databases, and technical literature

Excellent communication, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills

Ability to exercise sound independent judgment when working with limited information

A strong interest in technological advancement, innovation, and emerging technologies

This role may be offered as a full-time or part-time position depending on role/business needs and candidate availability; full-time positions are preferred and require working standard business hours in your local time zone

AI TUTOR, DESIGN - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by providing high-quality data annotations and inputs tailored to design contexts. You will leverage your expertise in fields such as graphic design, brand and visual design, product or UI/UX design, web design, game design, and illustration to support its training. You will evaluate, refine, and create design work so Grok can distinguish weak design from work that is clear, functional, and well-resolved. This work is grounded in design judgment, not software engineering or mastery of every medium.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Evaluate design outputs across formats, including visual assets, layouts, documents, websites, interactive prototypes, and/or games

Identify and clearly articulate design issues, including work that looks attractive but fails in use

Refine, restyle, or recreate outputs when they fall short, producing exceptionally strong examples

Write precise, well-reasoned annotations and critiques explaining the difference between mediocre, good, and excellent design

Help label high-quality datasets spanning graphic design, interface design, web experiences, game feel, and related design writing

Collaborate with technical staff on evaluation guidelines, rubrics, and examples that set a high bar for design quality

Work across a wide range of briefs and styles, from simple static pieces to complex interactive products, while staying consistent in quality and judgment

1+ years of professional experience (including freelance or contract work) in a design discipline such as graphic design, brand/visual design, product or UI/UX design, web design, game design, or illustration

Sharp eye for fundamentals (visual hierarchy, typography, spacing, color, composition, consistency, and clarity of communication)

Ability to evaluate design quality outside your primary specialty and clearly articulate what works, what does not, and why

Comfort creating high-quality reference examples, not only evaluating existing ones

Familiarity with accessibility and inclusive design principles

Working knowledge of modern design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, or equivalent

Experience with generative AI design tools and a clear point of view on when AI output looks generic, broken, or well-designed

Prior experience in design critique, art direction, QA, design review, data annotation, or AI evaluation

AI TUTOR, HUMANITIES - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by providing high-quality data annotations and inputs tailored to humanities contexts. You will leverage your expertise in fields such as linguistics, history, classical studies, literature, poetry, philosophy, ethics, visual arts, and performing arts to support its training. You will evaluate model outputs and create training data so Grok reasons accurately, weighs evidence carefully, and communicates uncertainty honestly. This work is grounded in scholarly judgment, not creative writing.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Evaluate model outputs in your field for factual accuracy, logical coherence, fallacious reasoning, and hidden assumptions

Flag confident-sounding errors, anachronism, misused sources, ideological slant, and claims that outrun the evidence

Create exemplary responses and datasets that show intellectual honesty, careful source evaluation, and a clear distinction between primary evidence, secondary interpretation, and speculation

Steel-man opposing views before criticizing them, and mark what is settled, contested, or unknown

Ground annotations and reference answers in primary sources whenever they exist, then weigh secondary scholarship against that record

Collaborate with technical staff to design evaluation guidelines, rubrics, and examples that test and strengthen Grok's behavior and personality in the humanities

Help define what good model behavior looks like in contested humanistic questions: precise, sourced, proportionately confident, and resistant to fashionable or motivated readings

POSITION DETAILS:

This is a temporary position with SpaceXSI, for the length of time as stated, and is subject to change with minimal notice as business needs dictate

LENGTH OF POSITION: 6 months (extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs)

LOCATION: Remote (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia); for US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree or higher in linguistics, history, classical studies, literature, poetry, philosophy, ethics, visual arts, performing arts, or an equivalent field

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

PhD in one of the listed fields, or equivalent demonstrated scholarly depth

Published analytical work, such as peer-reviewed articles, monographs, critical editions, catalog essays, or other rigorously sourced scholarship

Experience in teaching, academic peer review, archival research, textual criticism, historiography, or formal argument analysis

Range across more than one listed field, or across historically and culturally distinct canons within a field

Ability to assess arguments for validity, soundness, hidden premises, and category errors, not only for surface correctness

Excellent analytical writing in English: clear, precise, and calibrated to the strength of the evidence

Comfort working from evolving instructions to produce annotations, critiques, and reference answers at a consistently high standard

Familiarity with evaluating AI or LLM outputs, building benchmarks, or creating training data

Public writing or lectures that make difficult humanistic material accurate without flattening it

Design, develop, and manage facility automation projects from sequence of operations and control narrative through panel build, point-to-point checkout, commissioning, failover testing, and handoff to operations.

Integrate equipment controllers into the site BMS, EPMS, and historian so power, cooling, and environmental data are one operational picture.

Design control panels and electrical interfaces compliant with NEC, NFPA, and UL 508A, including motor and VFD interfaces, safety circuits, and network architecture.

Own the systems after go-live: alarm rationalization, loop tuning, sequence changes, outage support, and continuous improvement of uptime and energy performance.

Build schedules and punch lists for controls scope and drive vendors, contractors, and internal teams to hit them during construction and live expansions.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, controls, mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline.

1+ years of experience in industrial controls, building or plant automation, data center facilities, or related programming (internship and extracurricular experience applies).

Energized by fast, iterative design, construction, and commissioning on a live critical facility.

Proven ability to turn a messy plant problem into a simple, reliable control solution.

Clear written and verbal communication, including control narratives, sequences of operations, and recommendations across mechanical, electrical, and operations teams.

Judgment to move quickly while protecting people and equipment around high voltage, stored energy, refrigerants, fuel systems, and high-pressure hydronics.

Experience in data centers, power generation, district energy, industrial utilities, or other 24/7 process plants.

Experience in at least one of the disciplines below, with a real interest in learning the others.

Sizing and application of motors, VFDs, starters, valves, actuators, instrumentation, and circuit protection for pumps, fans, towers, and plant equipment.

Design of fail-safe circuits using safety relays and safety controllers, including interlocks that must hold during a loss of power or a controls failure.

Hands-on troubleshooting of industrial electrical systems with multimeters, oscilloscopes, and network diagnostics.

Reading and producing schematics, panel layouts, riser diagrams, and one-line diagrams (EPLAN preferred).

Fieldbus and Ethernet plant networks: BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, and OPC UA.

Designing, building, and commissioning control panels and electromechanical systems with arc-flash, lockout/tagout, and construction-power constraints in mind.

PLC programming in structured text and ladder, preferably Rockwell (Studio 5000), Siemens TIA Portal, or Beckhoff TwinCAT.

HMI, BMS, and SCADA development — Ignition, Niagara, or an equivalent platform — focused on fast navigation, meaningful alarms, trends, and equipment health.

Industrial protocols used in critical facilities: BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP, OPC UA, MQTT, SNMP, EtherNet/IP, and Profinet.

Experience with EPMS, power metering, generator or ATS status, and historian or alarming tools used to operate a data center.

CONSTRUCTION SCHEDULER

Develop, maintain, and communicate construction schedules that the field, subcontractors, and leadership can actually use. You will build CPM baselines, update them from real progress, flag risk early, and explain schedule impact of changes, delays, and recovery plans. This is not a data-entry role. You need enough means-and-methods knowledge to challenge a sequence that will not work in the field.

Superintendents run the work; project managers own cost and contracts; the scheduler is the person who can tell you what is actually driving the end date, what slips if a trade is late, and whether a recovery plan is real.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Build baseline CPM schedules from drawings, specs, estimates, bid packages, and construction sequences (WBS, activity coding, logic, calendars, and constraints used sparingly and correctly)

Maintain the live schedule: collect progress from superintendents, project managers, and trades; update percent complete, remaining duration, and logic; publish a clean current-period update on a set cadence (typically weekly look-aheads and monthly official updates)

Own the critical path. Identify near-critical work, float erosion, and out-of-sequence progress. Tell the team why the end date moved, not just that it did

Produce three-week (or similar) look-aheads that match the master schedule and what the field can actually crew

Analyze schedule impact of RFIs, change orders, design late-outs, access constraints, long-lead procurement, weather, and labor shortages. Prepare time-impact analyses (TIA) and what-if, recovery, and acceleration scenarios

Coordinate with project managers, superintendents, estimators, procurement, design, owners/CMs, and subcontractors so the schedule reflects committed dates, not wishful ones

Resource-load and, where required, cost-load the schedule. Flag crew stacking, craft shortages, and unrealistic production rates

Prepare narratives, variance reports, S-curves, histograms, and executive summaries for internal reviews and owner/CM submittals

Support claims and delay documentation with contemporaneous records (as-planned vs. as-built, fragnets, delay categorization) when needed

Enforce schedule standards: naming, coding, update process, backup, and version control so the file remains auditable

Facilitate or support pull-planning / Last Planner sessions and convert those commitments into logic in the CPM model

Visit the site regularly. A scheduler who never walks the job will be wrong

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

4+ years of construction scheduling on active projects (GC, CM, owner’s project controls, or specialty contractor)

4+ years of experience using Smartsheet, MS Project, or other project management tool

4+ years of experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Comfortability with multiple calendars, relationship types, filters, layouts, global vs. project data, and schedule quality checks (open ends, negative float, SS/FF overuse, constraints)

Bachelor’s in construction management, civil engineering, or a related field; OR equivalent field experience

PSP (AACE), PMI-SP, PMP, CCM, or similar credential

Experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics)

Forensic delay analysis, time-impact analysis, and claims support

Cost/resource loading, earned value, and integration with cost systems

Last Planner / pull planning; BIM 4D (Navisworks, Synchro) is a plus

Additional tools as applicable: Power BI, Smartsheet, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Willing to work extended hours as needed, including the current 6-day / 12-hour construction cadence

Must be comfortable working in a fully onsite environment

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SECURITY ENGINEER, KUBERNETES

We protect the platform that runs X and SpaceXSI. We don’t just report issues, we actively look for real risks and exploits in our Kubernetes environments and turn them into durable fixes and tooling. You will secure the platform behind X and SpaceXSI’s infrastructure, products, and workloads. If you know pod and platform security, think in attack paths, and want to build the defenses that make the platform safer at scale, we want to hear from you.

We value a understanding of how Kubernetes can actually be abused – not just how it is configured. We prioritize shipping practical controls and tooling over writing policy documents, applying least privilege and defense-in-depth at fleet scale, delivering clear findings and fixes that platform teams can act on, and conducting safe, constrained validation that does not put production at risk.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Secure the platform end to end: nodes, clusters, pods, roles, tokens, secrets, service-to-service communication, and the supply chain

Find and remediate overprivileged permissions, dangerous pod and workload settings, and escalation paths in operators, admission, networking, identity, and monitoring

Assess our own platform the way an adversary would, including container and pod breakout, privilege escalation, and movement across workloads, using safe and constrained validation, then fix what you find

Design and build security tooling and automation, including AI-assisted analysis, that catches risky configuration and overprivilege before or after it ships

Strengthen identity and secrets handling so workloads receive only the access they need

Improve supply-chain security through secure base images, continuous scanning, and related controls

Review changes that affect RBAC, operators, ServiceAccounts, network policies, and anything running with elevated privileges

Partner with platform and product teams as a security owner, taking problems from identification through rollout

Contribute to fleet-wide hardening, policy enforcement, and safer defaults

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

3+ years in platform security, Kubernetes security, or offensive security against production infrastructure

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Deep knowledge of pod and workload security: privileged containers, capabilities, host namespaces, host path mounts, service accounts, RBAC, admission control, and network isolation

Working knowledge of identity, secrets, workload identity, service-to-service trust, supply chain, runtime, and cloud access

Able to think like an attacker, measure blast radius, and turn the path into a detection, control, or tool

Comfortable with operators, custom resources, Helm, and GitOps workflows

Able to build or modify security tooling in Go, Python, or Rust when a control needs automation

Bonus: Image scanning, SBOMs, secure base images, policy-as-code (Kyverno, OPA), multi-cluster environments, runtime detection, and security testing of customer-facing application

Experience developing AI-driven security tools or integrating AI into security workflows

Familiarity with Kubernetes-based environments and securing cloud-native infrastructure

Proven ability to drive technical decisions and influence security practices across teams

A passion for challenging the status quo and building transformative security solutions

Strong collaboration skills, with experience working in dynamic, cross-functional teams

A sense of humor and adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Open to working out of one of our offices: Palo Alto, Austin, DC, or New York

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$100,000 - $198,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

SITE RELIABILITY ENGINEER

As a Site Reliability Engineer focused on campus reliability, you will design what the campus watches and trusts, technically command cross-discipline SEVs, and build the guardrails that make the next incident smaller. Own monitoring architecture and signal quality across GPU and host telemetry (DCGM, Prometheus/Grafana) and facility telemetry (BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, CDU / direct liquid cooling): what we alert on, suppress, and trust. Consume NOC noise-disposition feedback to drive suppression and redesign. Treat alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure

Provide SEV command support: technical incident leadership, bridge coordination with the NOC, paging and escalation (e.g., PagerDuty), and timeline and severity hygiene

Run blameless postmortems and drive corrective actions to closed, not filed

Gate high-risk change: fleet-scale firmware/BIOS/BMC rollouts (Redfish, canaries, rollback) and SOP/MOP/EOP-governed work on power and cooling systems through a disciplined change management process

Lead cross-functional reliability projects spanning compute, network (InfiniBand/RoCE), storage, and facility signal boundaries, including grey failures that cross those boundaries (e.g., NVLink flapping, thermal throttling, power sequencing)

Build and maintain playbooks, run game days, and keep cross-discipline dependency maps current. Own runbook quality jointly with the NOC (SRE designs; NOC operates and corrects)

Define error budgets and availability objectives at campus and service boundaries as adopted by the business

Demonstrate monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality

Treats alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure

Improve mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR) for severity-class events, and ensure blameless postmortems with closed action items.

Increase the alert actionable ratio and reduce recurrence of incident classes.

Expand monitoring coverage of critical dependencies across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling.

Minimize GPU fleet availability lost to infrastructure events.

Fleet firmware and BMC management (Redfish, IPMI), including firmware release validation and staged rollouts

Hands-on definition and use of SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets at service or campus boundaries
